newsitem.title: USA: National Registry launches fingerprint ID.
newsitem.headline: National Registry launches fingerprint ID.

text.p: National Registry Inc on Wednesday said it has introduced software that will allow consumers to use their finger-image, or fingerprints, to gain access to certain password-based systems.
NRIdentity Secure Authentication Facility for Windows NT, will sell for $199 per workstation. Windows NT is on operating system developed by Microsoft Corp.

The software allows users system access after they enter a User ID, then place an index finger on an NRIdentity Personal Authentication Desktop or Keyboard Scanner, which is not sold with the software, the St. Petersburg-based National Registry said.
The system verifies the user's identity and completes the log-on by delivering the password to the operating system.

The program also provides a "secure screen saver" feature capability that locks the keyboard and obscures the video monitor during a user's absence. A touch of a finger on the scanner "unlocks" the workstation, the company said.
National will market the software to firms requiring high degrees of assurance that only authorized users can access computer systems and networks containing sensitive data.
Microsoft, in a statement, noted that that it sees the technology adding popularity to its Windows NT system.
